correctness.rationale: The cost identity counts each edge once for every prefix before its first endpoint. For each fixed prefix length, minimizing remaining cross-edges reduces to maximizing a convex squared-sum under part-capacity bounds; the displayed two-part transfer proves the largest-capacity-first maximizer. The same smallest-part-first block ordering attains all prefix minima simultaneously, and summing its block contributions gives the formula. Exhaustive direct edge-time computation checks all 58 multipartite types through order eight and 925310 labeled orderings.

value.rationale: Complete multipartite graphs are the natural many-part extension of the complete bipartite family whose exact MSVC value was previously singled out. The theorem gives a closed form and a transparent optimal construction for every number of parts, not merely another algorithmic evaluation. It also supplies a structural benchmark for the recent vertex-cover-based study of the same ordering problem.
